newsitem.title: FINLAND: LOWER INTEREST RATES NO LONGER HELP BANKS - MERITA.
newsitem.headline: LOWER INTEREST RATES NO LONGER HELP BANKS - MERITA.

text.p: Lower interest rates would not help banks anymore and profitability will have to be boosted by better efficiency, said Vesa Vainio, CEO of Finland's largest banking group Merita Oy .
"Lower interest rates do no longer improve banks' results," Vainio told a seminar late on Tuesday.
Other income will rise, but slowly, he said.

"The increase in other income will be modest, and therefore cost efficiency will have to be improved," Vainio said, adding he was convinced that Merita would reach an internationally competitive level in a couple of years.
He declined to comment on the ongoing restructuring in the Nordic banking industry.

Vainio repeated an earlier estimate that Merita's costs if Finland joins Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) would be some 200 million markka in 1997 to 2002 while the net loss of income in EMU would be 200 million to 300 million markka a year.
